chunks: That Abā al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام used to awaken from his sleep, then perform wudu (ablution), and not perform istinjāʾ. And he said, as one expressing astonishment, about a man whom he named: “It has reached me that when wind comes out from him, he performs istinjāʾ.”

key_terms.بَلَغَنِي: it reached me; I was informed
key_terms.يَسْتَنْجِي: he performs istinja, cleansing the private area after impurity

ai.seo_question: Does passing wind require istinja or only wudu in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith reports that Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام would perform wudu (ablution) after waking from sleep without performing istinjāʾ, and that he expressed astonishment at someone who would perform istinjāʾ after passing wind. The report relates to rulings and etiquette concerning ritual purity and what necessitates washing after relieving oneself.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.65 - It was narrated that Abu Al-Hasan Imam Ali ibn Musa Ar-Ridha (as) would awaken from his sleep, perform ablution, and not perform istinja.
He expressed astonishment at a man whom he referred to, saying, "I have heard that when he passes gas, he performs istinja."
